chunks: From it: O creature who has been equitably created, and who has been nurtured in the darkness of the wombs, and behind multiple veils,
You were originated from [an essence of] clay,
And placed in a firm resting place,
to a known measure and an appointed time. You move in the womb of your mother as an embryo, neither understanding a call, nor hearing a summons,
ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the creation of man in the womb?
ai.summary: Imam Ali addresses the human soul as a distinct entity ('al-makhluq al-sawi') that precedes the body, highlighting the metaphysical journey from clay to the womb. This passage underscores the Shia concept of the soul's pre-existence and its gradual descent into material form, illustrating the divine wisdom behind human vulnerability and dependence on God during embryonic development.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [A part of the same sermon (about man’s creation, and pointing towards the requirements of life) :] O creature who has been equitably created and who has been nurtured and looked after in the darkness of wombs with multiple curtains.
You were originated from the essence of clay (Qur’ān, 23:12) and placed in a still place for a known length (Qur’ān, 77:21-22) and an ordained time.
You used to move in the womb of your mother as an embryo, neither responding to a call nor hearing any voice.
